headline: Cyclone Arnab forms over Bay, expected to cross India on Wednesday
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has issued distant warning signal No. 2 for several maritime ports as the storm intensifies.
details: A deep depression in the east-central Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD).
The storm is currently moving west-northwestwards and is expected to become a severe cyclonic storm by midnight on Monday.
It is projected to further intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra coast of India on Wednesday.
The maximum sustained wind speed within 54km of the cyclone's centre is approximately 62kmph, with gusts or squalls reaching up to 88kmph.
The BMD has advised the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No. 2.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been warned to remain close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.
The name 'Arnab', meaning sea or ocean, was proposed by Bangladesh as part of a regional naming process involving 13 countries.
caption:
Cyclone Arnab has formed over the Bay of Bengal and is heading toward India's coast.

A deep depression in the east-central Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD).

The storm is currently moving west-northwestwards and is expected to become a severe cyclonic storm by midnight on Monday.

It is projected to further intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra coast of India on Wednesday.

The maximum sustained wind speed within 54km of the cyclone's centre is approximately 62kmph, with gusts or squalls reaching up to 88kmph.

The BMD has advised the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No. 2.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been warned to remain close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.

The name 'Arnab', meaning sea or ocean, was proposed by Bangladesh as part of a regional naming process involving 13 countries.

headline_marked: [[Shilpakala Academy bomb blast]] suspect arrested; police say he was linked to banned student group
headline: Shilpakala Academy bomb blast suspect arrested; police say he was linked to banned student group
summary: Police have arrested the main suspect in connection with a cocktail explosion outside the Shilpakala Academy. The arrested individual is identified as Abul Hayat Dipu, reportedly a member of a banned student organization.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) announced the arrest of the primary suspect in a case related to a cocktail explosion near the Shilpakala Academy in the capital. The arrested individual has been identified as Abul Hayat Dipu.
According to DMP's press release, Dipu is a member of a banned student organization. The explosion occurred on September 20, and Dipu was named the main accused in the subsequent case.

Details regarding the exact date and location of Dipu's arrest were not provided in the DMP's announcement. Further investigation is ongoing to determine the full extent of his involvement and any potential accomplices.
caption:
Main suspect in Shilpakala Academy bomb blast arrested.
Police say he was a member of a banned student group.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) announced the arrest of the primary suspect in a case related to a cocktail explosion near the Shilpakala Academy in the capital. The arrested individual has been identified as Abul Hayat Dipu.

According to DMP's press release, Dipu is a member of a banned student organization. The explosion occurred on September 20, and Dipu was named the main accused in the subsequent case.

Details regarding the exact date and location of Dipu's arrest were not provided in the DMP's announcement. Further investigation is ongoing to determine the full extent of his involvement and any potential accomplices.
